name: killall
summary: Sends a signal to every process with a given name.
description: Like kill, but targets processes by name rather than by PID: every matching instance receives the signal. The default signal is SIGTERM (clean stop). The name must match the program name exactly; for a looser search, see pkill.

options.description: Signal to send, by name or number (HUP, KILL, 9…).
Asks for confirmation before each process.
Reports whether the signal was sent.
Waits for every targeted process to finish.
Ignores the case of the name.

example.output: HUP INT QUIT ILL TRAP ABRT BUS FPE KILL USR1 SEGV USR2 PIPE ALRM TERM

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Exact name of the target program(s).

examples.explanation: Asks every Firefox window to close cleanly.
Forces every chrome process to stop.
Asks nginx to reload its configuration.
Stops esprit’s python3 processes, asking for confirmation for each one.

dangerNote: killall targets every instance of a program, including those in other sessions when run with sudo. Check with ps or pgrep first.
